html:
The Shiwilu, also called Jeberos, are an Indigenous people of the Loreto region of the Peruvian Amazon, centred on the town of Jeberos, between the Marañón and Huallaga rivers. Their language belongs to the small Cahuapanan family.

In the 1600s Jesuits founded a mission at Jeberos, part of the missions of Maynas, and it became a base for spreading into the region. Over the following centuries Spanish took over as the everyday language, and today only a few elders speak Shiwilu fluently, though there are efforts to teach it again. They live in Peru, near the Kichwa Lamista.
